sections.name: anti-cheat in the Lock API (anticheat)
sections.title: Anti-cheat rules
sections.what: Checks one pick per call, burst flags that log without blocking, no repeated logging of old bursts, safe behaviour when logging fails, and no flags for normal play.
sections.why: Likely reason: detect suspicious activity for review while never blocking honest players automatically.
sections.watch_out: Logger spies are restored at the end of tests, so a failure before that can affect later tests.

summary: Tests the lab's anti-cheat rules: one pick per call, burst detection that logs for review without blocking, and logging failures that never stop a saved lock.
purpose: Protects the fairness rules and checks that flagging is safe for users.
why: Likely reason: the lab should spot suspicious rapid picks for a human to review, not punish users automatically.
how: Resets the database. Checks a second lock on the same call is refused as a conflict. Checks ten locks in a minute raise a burst flag and log a warning. Checks an old burst is not logged again, and a failing logger only logs an error without failing the lock. Checks a few spaced-out calls have no flags.
inputs: Real moments from the lab service, test users, and spies on the logger.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The tests replace logger methods with spies and restore them afterwards. A failure before the restore could leak the spy into later tests.
debug: If the burst test fails, check the flag kinds the integrity check returns. If the logging test fails, check the messages sent to the logger.
